channel.title: Epilog
channel.description: Updates for the Epilog macOS app

item.title: Epilog 1.1
item.description:
Features

  • Easier to recognize sessions and breaks in the circle timer. Breaks have their own dots, and the long break replaces the dots with a single cup.
  • Live Activity and Dynamic Island. iPhone and iPad now provide a timer Live Activity, as well as a Dynamic Island on iPhone. Skip, stop, pause, add five minutes, or go straight into your break without opening the app.
  • Mac keyboard shortcuts. ⌘N for a new entry; ⌘S, ⌘↩, or Return twice to save it; ⌘1, ⌘2, ⌘3 for Today, My Days, and Settings; Space, ←, and → run the timer.
  • Add new entries from anywhere in your journal. The New Entry button is now in the toolbar. My Days has one too: the entry starts on that day, and if you're looking at a specific category it will apply that category by default.
  • More glass timers: Clear, Aviator, Frosted, and Classic. Frosted is the new default. Requires macOS 26 or iOS 26.
  • Autocorrect and spell-check in the entry sheet. On iPhone and iPad the keyboard corrects as you type. Typos are now underlined on all platforms.

Improvements

  • Entry sheet clean-up.
  • A "Ready" timer shows you the ready interval, not the "next" interval.
  • Countdown time doesn't bounce around anymore, and durations under ten minutes read as 9:59, not 09:59.
  • Short breaks and long breaks each have their own switch. When hourly check-ins and hourly breaks land on the same minute, you choose which break to keep instead of losing the short one.
  • Interval settings provide time examples. Timer settings now list your next four check-ins and next two breaks as clock times, to make it easier to understand the check-in, end of session, and start of session settings.
  • The circle timer's parallax animation on iPhone has been improved. Reduce Motion turns the movement off.
  • iPad has @ and # keys on the main keyboard.
  • Icons have changed for User Guide, Settings, New Entry, Edit Categories, and AI Refresh.
  • Claude API defaults to Claude Opus 5 and supports Workspace ID.
  • OpenAI API is ready for Astra.

Fixes

  • Sign in with Apple and Google accounts can be deleted from inside the app. Before, the confirmation required a password. Now it confirms using the sign-in you used.
  • The "Key Needed" alert can open Settings, instead of telling you to DIY.
  • On iPad, the AI summary error alert stays long enough to read.
  • In the Mac Delete Account sheet, Return backs out. Deleting takes a deliberate click.

item.title: Epilog 1.0
item.description:
Features

  • Version 1.0 release! This is a feature-full release, ready for you early birds. iPhone and iPad now being tested in TestFlight. Private testing for now, but if you're in the circle, you can now use Epilog on Mac, iPhone, and iPad.
  • Select and copy a whole day. Entries are now selectable text — drag across as many as you like, ⌘A, ⌘C, or look a word up. Paste into anything and it arrives formatted.
  • Tap a tag to see everywhere you've used it. Click any #tag or @mention in an entry and Epilog jumps to My Days with that tag selected and the list filtered to it.
  • Copied summaries carry an attribution. When you copy a full summary, it ends with a one-line "— made by Epilog" that links back to the site. Copying a single bullet or a short phrase doesn't add it. Opt-out in Settings → Summaries → Clipboard.
  • Your day's tags, ordered by where you spent the most time. My Days used to list tags alphabetically across two lines, so sometimes the tags that mattered most were getting cut out. They now sit on one line, most-effort tags first.

Improvements

  • A slightly better app icon. P3 colors, instead of old sRGB.
  • Opens straight into your journal. Epilog no longer waits on the network to work out who you are at launch — including offline, where it used to bounce you to the sign-in screen and back.
  • Signing in happens on auth.epilog.io. The browser sheet now shows our own domain instead of a generic vendor address.
  • Terms and Privacy, where you'd expect them. Linked from the sign-in and sign-up screens, Settings → Privacy, Settings → Legal, and the Help menu.
  • The timer's completion notification tells you what's next. It now carries the same "Next: 5 min break" line the ring shows.
  • Category rows respond to a click anywhere on the row. Previously only the label was clickable.

Fixes

  • No more AI summary glitches. Generated summaries are checked before they're saved — if a model returns placeholder or garbled output, Epilog retries once and then leaves your existing summary exactly where it was.
  • Pasted summaries no longer garble punctuation. Copying a summary into Notes or Mail could turn spaces and dashes into mojibake. Fixed.
  • My Days shows which day is selected again. The highlight had been painted over since the first build.
  • A revoked sign-in signs you out. If your session is ended elsewhere, Epilog returns you to the sign-in screen instead of running on a dead identity.
  • On the Mac, entries are selected by dragging. A single click now opens an entry for editing, so double-click no longer selects a word.

item.title: Epilog 0.21
item.description:
Your journal is now end-to-end encrypted. 0.21 rebuilds sync on a new account system with true end-to-end encryption: entries are sealed on your Mac before they leave it, and only you hold the key. We couldn't read your journal if we wanted to.

  • Sign in with Apple, Google, or email — accounts are new in 0.21, so everyone starts fresh
  • A new Mac unlocks your journal automatically through iCloud Keychain — or with your recovery key, which Epilog helps you save when your account is created
  • Reset your password right in the app with an emailed 6-digit code; changing it signs out your other devices and sends a confirmation email

Back up and restore. Settings → Journal Backup now exports your whole journal to a file — and imports it back. Import is additive, with a preview: it can restore accidentally deleted entries, and it asks before merging matching categories.

A better daily quote. The Today screen's quote is now a real, attributed quote, with a tone that follows the arc of the week. Repeats are impossible, and pooled quotes work even offline.

Extra Time keeps its promise. The timer's +5 now defers your break instead of skipping it — when you're ready, the break runs in full.

Design

  • A new app icon
  • Entry lists restyled for reading: softer body text, quieter timestamps, tags that stand out
  • Summaries: create any timeframe from the "+" sheet — one summary per period, with a "Last updated" footer showing what wrote it
  • More consistent backgrounds in light and dark; the tint color setting is retired

Fixes

  • Report a Bug now delivers reliably, even when written offline
  • First sign-in sync hardening; uncategorized entries from older journals appear in the Uncategorized bucket again

item.title: Epilog 0.20
item.description:
The User Guide is here. Epilog now has a full User Guide at epilog.io/user-guide — every screen, feature, and setting explained, and always up to date. It's one tap away in Settings and in the Mac's Help menu.

Working past midnight? Epilog keeps up. When a work session runs through midnight, Today now shows a live "Tonight so far" summary of the whole session — last night and this morning together. It refreshes on demand and retires on its own once the session ends. (Requires AI summaries to be enabled.)

Categories, right where you use them. Add, rename, recolor, reorder, or delete your categories directly in the Categories drawer, instead of in the Settings page.

Settings and Help, reorganized. Settings are now grouped so things sit where you'd look — including new direct links to the online User Guide. The Mac Help menu now offers a variety of support options; Help & Support (⌘?) routes right into the app.

Timer settings, live. Changes apply immediately — even to a running timer. An active session will re-grid into the new rhythm on the spot; a break already underway will finish as expected. Timer settings are global, so settings will automatically refresh when another device changes your cycle.

Small improvements

  • Day pages in My Days show the day's time range in the header — "Sunday · 9:21 PM – 11:30 PM."
  • Summary cost estimates track current provider pricing and the newest models' tokenizers.

Fixes

  • The summary pill bar no longer shows a horizontal scroll bar when system scroll bars are set to Automatic or Always.
  • Entries that end exactly at midnight now appear only on the day they started — matching how a late night actually feels.
  • Entry timestamps are now consistently whole-minute everywhere — no more stray seconds sneaking in from edits or connected tools.

Under the hood

  • Sync hardening: the last legacy migration path now uses the same clobber-proof write pattern as the rest of sync.
  • Release and update infrastructure groundwork for test/beta update channels.

item.title: Epilog 0.19
item.description:
A new look on macOS 26

  • Epilog takes on Liquid Glass — a soft glass backdrop behind your day, with controls that float on the new material.
  • The circle timer becomes a glass lens with a floating shadow, tuned by hand until it caught the light just right.
  • Prefer the classic look? Two new settings — Timer and Timer background — let you choose Glass or Classic.
  • On earlier versions of macOS, everything keeps its familiar chrome.

Privacy

  • Epilog now collects anonymous usage statistics — which features get used, never what you write. Your entries, tags, and summaries stay yours. Opt out any time in Settings → Privacy.
  • Removed the unused Firebase Analytics library and added Apple's privacy manifest, so what the app declares is exactly what it does.

Polish

  • Summary pages read better: full-size text in the standard text color, categories in the order you arranged them, and padding that lines up with the Entries page.
  • The summary refresh button now wears Epilog's AI mark.

item.title: Epilog 0.18
item.description:
Summaries, beyond the day

  • My Days now has dedicated Summary views — flip between your entries and AI summaries with a tap
  • Summaries now span real stretches of time: week, two-week, month, quarter, half-year, and year, anchored to whichever day you're viewing
  • Cleaner summary layout: a quick overview up top, then each journal in its own section
  • Each journal's section pairs a short overview with bullet highlights

AI that asks first

  • Long-duration summaries (a month or longer) are generated only when you ask, with token and cost estimates and a confirmation dialog before you commit. They are never auto-generated.
  • Every summary page shows when it was last updated and a freshness icon
  • Long generations are now far more reliable — no more silently stalled summaries

Fixes and improvements

  • Fixed a scrolling freeze in Today on macOS
  • Fixed list spacing in Today on iOS
  • Connected agents can now write day and period summaries over MCP

item.title: Epilog 0.17
item.description:
What's new

  • A rebuilt timer. The focus timer now runs on a rewritten engine — pause and resume land exactly where you left off, the "previous" button behaves predictably, and countdowns stay honest across every interval and break.
  • Grace time. When a session ends, you can add five more minutes without losing your place — and if you run extra-extra time we extend your entry duration.
  • Your reminder, your schedule. Pick the time of day and the specific weekdays you want to be nudged to write. Night owls are covered — evenings run late into the early morning.
  • Report a bug or share feedback, in-app. A new Report a Bug / Feature Request / Feedback option sends your note straight to us — no email client required.

Fixes

  • Offline edits no longer get clobbered. Entries written while you're offline now sync back field-by-field instead of overwriting the whole day, and a sync indicator shows when your data is safely saved. Epilog also recovers on its own from silent sync failures.
  • Smaller cleanups across navigation and the day views for a steadier, more consistent feel.

item.title: Epilog 0.16
item.description:
AI summaries, your choice of provider

  • Connect ChatGPT using your own OpenAI API key — alongside the existing Claude API support
  • Your AI preferences now follow your account, and API keys are kept separate per account
  • Summaries now speak in your own voice and stay shorter and more scannable

A cleaner Settings window

  • Settings reorganized into grouped sections, in the style of macOS System Settings
  • Full open-source license texts are now included

Fixes

  • Fixed the auto-updater failing to start when the app was in the foreground from launch
  • Fixed the summary progress spinner clipping in the toolbar
  • AI status rows no longer appear while AI services are turned off

item.title: Epilog 0.15
item.description:
Instantly Summarize Your Day using AI

  • Epilog can now write a professional summary of your day: a short overview plus a breakdown for each category, updated automatically as you add entries.
  • Summaries are generated on your Mac with Apple Intelligence (macOS 26) — your entries never leave the device.
  • Summary text is fully selectable and pastes as clean text into Slack, Notes, or anywhere else — ready for stand-ups.
  • A new Enable AI Services switch turns all of it off in one place.

Bring Your Own Claude

  • Prefer a cloud model? Add your Anthropic API key and summaries are generated by Claude instead — using any model available with your key, including effort levels.
  • Works on any Mac, including ones without Apple Intelligence. Entries are sent to Anthropic only when Claude is selected, and usage is billed to your key.

Timer

  • The Previous button on a break now restarts the break first; press it again to step back an interval.

Fixes and refinements

  • Window size and position are remembered as separate settings, so Today keeps its own window frame separate from My Days and Settings.
  • Fixed a rare issue where custom categories could be replaced by the starter set.
  • Smoother category menu show/hide animation in My Days.

item.title: Epilog 0.14
item.description:
Autocomplete for tags & mentions

  • Start typing # or @ in an entry and Epilog suggests your most-used tag right in the text — press Tab or → to accept it, ↑/↓ to browse other matches
  • Suggestions are scoped to the journal you're writing in, so each category offers its own tags

Tags, everywhere they belong

  • Tags from your past entries now show up reliably in tag clouds and filters — including older entries where they'd previously gone missing
  • Tags and mentions display in a softer tone that stays out of the way of your writing

Windows that remember

  • Each view — timer, My Days, Settings — keeps its own window size and position, and switching views glides the window into place

Account

  • Change your password anytime from Settings → My Account

item.title: Epilog 0.13
item.description:
Find Your #Tags & @Mentions

  • Every journal in the sidebar now shows a tag cloud for #tags and @mentions — now it's easier to discover what you've been writing about at a glance, and jump straight to any tag.
  • Tags now carry their journal's color throughout your days and entries.

Weeks that start on Monday

  • Weeks now follow the ISO standard — Monday through Sunday — consistently on every device and in every region.
  • Weeks around New Year's are labeled correctly: late-December days that belong to the new year's first week now say so.
  • Your journal reorganizes itself automatically the first time you launch this version — nothing for you to do.

item.title: Epilog 0.12
item.description:
Smoother, faster, and better through the night.

  • Overnight sessions get their due. Entries that cross midnight now show up on both days — finish at 1:30 AM and you'll find the entry under yesterday and this morning. Time labels adapt the way Messages does: "Yesterday 11:00 PM – Today 1:30 AM" today, "Fri, Jul 10 11:00 PM – Sat, Jul 11 1:00 AM" when you look back later.
  • Your category sticks. New entries now default to the last category you used — including after relaunching Epilog.
  • No more stutters. Fixed the hangs that could freeze the countdown, the menu bar timer, and scrolling. Epilog stays responsive even with years of journal history.
  • Steadier at launch. Fixed the most common crash — starting a second copy of Epilog while one was already running.
  • Sharper AI connections. Agents logging your work over MCP can now use precise timestamps, so late-night entries land on the right day.

item.title: Epilog 0.11
item.description:
Epilog 0.11

Deleting is no longer forever. Deleted entries — whether removed by you or by a connected AI app — are now recoverable for 30 days instead of being erased immediately. AI apps get a matching restore ability, and previous versions of edited entries are kept.

AI apps now work under guardrails. Every entry records who wrote it — you, or a specific AI app on a specific device. AI apps must prove they've read an entry before they can delete it, you decide how many entries one AI conversation may delete (Settings → AI Connections), and every AI change is logged on your Mac.

Smarter AI journaling. Connected AI apps can now log entries that cross midnight, add to an existing time block without creating duplicates, give each line its own category, review any span of your journal — a quarter, a year, all of it — and verify exactly which Epilog they're talking to.

Fixes

  • Overnight entries that end after midnight no longer show "(Yesterday)" beside a time that's already today.
  • Repeated #hashtags and @mentions in a single entry are no longer counted twice.
  • AI connections stay responsive while the app is busy, and simultaneous AI edits can no longer overwrite each other.

item.title: Epilog 0.10
item.description:
Connect your AI apps

Epilog can now act as an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, letting AI apps on your Mac work with your journal — Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and any other MCP-capable app. They can search and read your entries, log new ones for you, and write day and week summaries.

  • Turn it on in Settings → AI Connections, then copy the setup snippet for your AI app.
  • Off by default. Connections only work while Epilog is running and signed in, and you can turn them off anytime.
  • Once enabled, a status button appears in the toolbar: green while the server is running. Click it to toggle AI Connections without opening Settings.

User Guide (in progress)

Epilog now has a built-in User Guide. Mac users can now open it from the Help menu or press ⌘?. It includes step-by-step AI Connections setup and a full command reference. More topics are on the way.

item.title: Epilog 0.9
item.description:
What's New

  • Entry Editor: press Up button to reuse prior entries
  • Epilog on macOS can now look for and install updates — on by default, opt out in Settings → General
  • A Download button will show when updates are available
  • Sign in with Apple or Google added

Bug Fixes

  • Tint colors
  • Various layouts
  • Various fixes in the iPhone & iPad apps
